title: ER Modeling Exercise
description: Given a business scenario (online bookstore), produce a complete ER diagram. Identify entities, relationships, cardinalities, and participation constraints. Convert to a relational schema in 3NF.

title: SQL Fundamentals
description: Write SQL queries against a provided university database. Includes: multi-table joins, subqueries, aggregation with GROUP BY and HAVING, and basic string/date functions.

title: Advanced SQL and Query Optimization
description: Write queries using window functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG/LEAD), CTEs, and recursive queries. Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to evaluate query plans. Add indexes and measure performance improvement.

title: Transaction Isolation Lab
description: Using a provided multi-user simulation script, observe and document the effects of different transaction isolation levels (READ UNCOMMITTED through SERIALIZABLE). Identify phantom reads, dirty reads, and non-repeatable reads in your observations.

title: Database Administration Basics
description: Set up a PostgreSQL instance. Configure user roles and permissions. Write a backup script using pg_dump. Set up a monitoring query to identify slow queries from pg_stat_statements.

title: Midterm Exam
description: Written exam covering ER modeling, normalization theory (1NF through BCNF), relational algebra, SQL query writing, and transaction concepts (ACID properties, isolation levels).

title: Final Exam
description: Comprehensive written exam. Includes all midterm topics plus: query optimization, indexing strategies, NoSQL concepts and tradeoffs, CAP theorem, and database administration.

title: Group Database Project
description: Teams of 3-4 design and implement a database-backed application. Deliverables: ER diagram, normalized schema (3NF minimum), 10+ sample queries demonstrating joins/aggregation/subqueries, brief written report analyzing design tradeoffs and what you'd change.
